#1845. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1844. Michael Carrick urged Manchester United to sign Chelsea star on his four-player shortlist

Michael Carrick urged Manchester United to sign Morgan Rogers ahead of Chelsea in the summer transfer window, according to reports.

Carrick was sacked by United on Thursday morning, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be appointed ahead of the team’s next Premier League game away to Liverpool on November 22.

After Sunday’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United sit 18th in the Premier League and are already out of the Carabao Cup after they were beaten by Brighton in September.

Carrick was forced to contend with several injury headaches during his final weeks in charge as United were without Luke Shaw and a recognised striker with Benjamin Sesko sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

United opted to focus on strengthening their midfield options in the summer and spent £155 million on signing Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

According to The Telegraph, Carrick was ‘far from happy’ with United’s business in the summer transfer window and all four of his recommendations to the club’s hierarchy failed to materialise.

The report claims that Carrick wanted Rogers, who he had already managed at Middlesborough, and was ‘convinced’ that the 24-year-old wanted to make the move to United.

However, United’s hierarchy refused to enter a bidding war with Chelsea, who ended up signing Rogers in a £117m deal from Aston Villa.

Carrick also wanted United to sign Elliot Anderson, who moved to Manchester City for £116m, and had also recommended Mateus Fernandes, who joined Tottenham Hotspur for £85m after United refused to meet West Ham’s valuation.

United were also targeting a new left-back and Carrick’s preference was to sign Lewis Hall from Newcastle United but United’s approach in the summer window was quickly rejected.

Meanwhile, Gary Neville has urged Pochettino to seek guarantees over the club’s transfer activity in the next two transfer windows before accepting to take the United job.

‘He needs two defenders in January. So he’s got to insist that he gets two defenders in January,’ Neville said on Stick to Football.

‘He’s got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around. He’s got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

‘They have to give it to him, or else he shouldn’t take the job. If you are not going to give them a look without that defence and that midfield, by the way, and that midfield has some money spent on it, he’s got to insist on the way in there’s some form of transfer control, there’s some sort of budget where he can meaningfully change the team.’

#1842. Sheffield Wednesday 3 Plymouth 0: A win's a win as Owls get Dave Challinor up and running without sparkling

After six games without a win and back-to-back cup defeats to start Challinor's managerial reign, it did not matter how they beat Plymouth Argyle, just that they did.

A 3-0 win with goals from the excellent Billy Mitchell, Davis Keillor-Dunn and a brilliant individual goal from Di'Shon Bernard flattered Wednesday.

None of the home fans in the 29,228 will have cared.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

With only a patchy schedule in international week, they are back in the League One play-off places and above Plymouth on goal difference.

Wednesday were very poor in the first half until taking the lead just as it came to the end. They matched the Pilgrims in the second half without blowing them away.

The atmosphere for Challinor's first home league game was pretty flat for the first hour, with the team failing to get the Hillsborough crowd excited.

The Owls' first-half football was as low-key as Challinor's introduction to the crowd, Plymouth's football not as bright as their luminous orange kit and certainly not on a par with the annoying pitchside advertising hoardings, but much better than Wednesday's in the opening 44 minutes.

Starting in a shape which flitted between 4-2-3-1 and 3-2-4-1 as Sil Swinkels tucked in and Yan Valery pushed on in possession, the Owls struggled to keep the ball and therefore pose any attacking threat to a team who, like them, have promotion ambitions and a long injury list.

Jaden Heskey being caught on the ball in the ninth minute summed up the hosts' slackness and he was fortunate Callum Slattery tracked back and made a penalty-area tackle which had to be perfectly timed.

Roman Curtis had a shot saved by the fit-again Joe Lumley in the tenth minute after Xavier Amaechi nutmegged Swinkels in the build up. The ball was bundled behind for a corner Lumley flapped at but Will Evans could only cushion his volley from it into the side netting.

A lovely ball from Malachi Boateng found Bradley Ibrahim, but Lumley came off his line to save. Evans shot at the goalkeeper when picked out.

Bernard was hassled into an error in the 37th minute but made up for it with some good defending when the ball came in, just as he made a good recovery tackle when Amaechi threatened to force his way through.

In between time, Ibrahim missed a woeful chance, thrashing at fresh air rather than the ball Amaechi laid on for him. The far-post header Amaechi put wide in the 63rd minute would equal it for wastefulness.

That said, Plymouth had a reprieve in the 17th minute when Curtis planted his studs into the chest of Jamal Lowe, but only received a yellow card.

As half-time approached, Wednesday had only had a couple of half-chances, Mitchell's first-time wall pass finding Keillor-Dunn on the counter-attack but his ball to Barry Bannan giving Wes Harding the chance to make a brilliant slide tackle.

Slattery's excellent pass found Mitchell in the 35th minute, but, forced wide, he could only win a corner.

But the Owls delivered right at the end of the half.

Bernard thought he had scored from a corner, only for Ibrahim to nod his goalbound effort over the bar and when former Owls loanee touched the next one to Mitchell, his shot took a big deflection on its way in.

The sides matched each other chance for chance at the start of the second half.

A quick throw-in set up Keillor-Dunn for a shot that was blocked, and when Plymouth counter-attacked, the same fate befell Ibrakim's effort.

With the crowd sensing the part they had to play, just after the hour Keillor-Dunn released Lowe to weave his way through and force a save. The ball came back to Keillor-Dunn, who really ought to have hit the target. So should Amaechi with his header a minute later.

Louie Barry had an early chance to mark his first appearance since September 1 with a goal, but leant back on his shot.

Two goals in as many minutes put the doubts out of minds, though.

The first came when Plymouth defended a Slattery free-kick awfully, and Keillor-Dunn popped up to poke hme a centre-forward's goal, his sixth of the season.

If he was an entirely predictable scorer, Bernard was not.

The centre-back loves to barrel forward from time to time but it rarely ends with a finish as good as the one he hit in off a post after what turned out to be a one-two in his own half with Boateng's sliding tackle and just carrying on.

It papered over a few cracks, but no matter.

#1841. Cisse sheds light on Mancini’s call, impressions of Italy camp and Milan Scudetto desire

Alphadjo Cisse did his first press conference as a member of the senior Italian national team, responding to questions on a number of topics.

Cisse has been called up for the first time by Roberto Mancini, having made a sensational start to the season in his first year in Serie A, which came after recovering from a serious muscle injury that kept him out for the entire second half of last season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The 20-year-old has already scored eight goals across all competitions, with five coming in the league. The most recent of these was against Genoa on Sunday, and now there is talk of a renewal offer from Milan in order to reward his development but also fend off interest from the Premier League.

Cisse spoke at a press conference from the Azzurri headquarters at Coverciano, alongside former Milan man Mattia Liberali, with whom he played in Catanzaro. His comments were relayed by TMW.

What are your feelings after the last few months?

“I always want to demonstrate my qualities. I’ve had some very intense months and I hope to have many more like them.”

What are the strengths and weaknesses of Liberali?

“His play, his shooting. His final pass is one of his best qualities. As for his flaws, I’d say he’s a bit touchy.”

Did you expect to be the top scorer among Italian players?

“Last year’s injury was a difficult time, but I handled it well. I was very confident about coming to Milanello to showcase my skills, and that helped me a lot. Choosing Catanzaro in 2025 was a very easy decision. Polito and Aquilani wanted me, and it was the right choice. I needed playing time.”

“I can play anywhere in attack. As for the specific role, I don’t know if it’s better to say. I like playing in all positions.”

What impression did entering Coverciano give you?

“It’s great to be here, a great responsibility. We’ll have the opportunity to get to know each other in the coming days.”

“My teammates welcomed me very well, but there’s certainly a big difference between Serie B and Serie A. I owe Aquilani a lot, he’s given me a lot and given me a lot of confidence. I’m sorry for him [after he was sacked by Sassuolo], but he’ll definitely have a great coaching career.”

You’re more about talent than physicality, is anything changing?

“Quality is always important. Now in Italy, many young players are emerging, and we’re trying to give them more confidence.”

“For Milan, winning is the priority, the Scudetto like any other competition. Winning is the norm and you can’t neglect any competition. At Milan you have to win everything.”

“Every coach has left me with something. Aquilani had a huge impact last year. Mancini? He welcomed me and encouraged me to train well. Baldini helped me a lot, even though I only worked with him for two weeks. He left me with a lot.”

“Modric would be too obvious… I say Gila.”

Are you aiming to start at San Siro against France?

“The coach will decide. I’m a guy with a lot of ambition, and being here with the national team is a source of pride.”

What kind of game do you expect against France?

“They need no introduction, but Italy always aims to win. Qualifying for Italy should be the norm.”

“Without a doubt, Balotelli, he’s always been a point of reference for me in the national team.”

Do you feel ready to be a point of reference here right away?

“I like pressure, and I think I’ve got the strength to handle it. There are some important players here, some of them have won the European Championship, and you have to show respect. You have to take things one step at a time. The first thing to focus on is making your debut, and then we’ll see.”

#1839. Hearts boss Vrancken is playing with fire by turning the guns on his own players

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:17 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 12:26 EST, 10 November 2026

Not for the first time this season under Wouter Vrancken, Hearts suffered a complete and utter implosion as they were thrashed 5-2 at home to Falkirk last weekend.

This is a team who lost 6-0 to Sturm Graz over two legs in the Champions League qualifiers back at the start of the campaign.

A team who were then battered 6-1 away against Benfica in Lisbon in the Europa League qualifiers – and a team who were also thumped 7-1 against Celtic at Parkhead a few weeks ago.

Hearts also lost the derby to Hibs just over a week ago in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup at Hampden.

Now comes an annihilation against Falkirk where Hearts were 4-0 down by half-time. What a shambolic way to lose a long unbeaten record at home.

Even accounting for what had gone before in some of those matches this season, what happened on Sunday at Tynecastle felt like a new low.

Hearts were a shambles. But what was even more alarming was the manager's inability to stop the bleeding and make any changes from the touchline.

All of which poses a very simple question. Have Hearts and Jamestown made a mistake with Vrancken? At the moment, he looks hopelessly one-dimensional.

But it was his post-match comments on Sunday afternoon which actually became even more alarming than the performance itself.

Wouter Vrancken was 'embarrassed' by Hearts' 5-2 home loss to Falkirk

Vrancken branded it 'embarrassing' and a 'disgrace'. He called his players 'childish' and basically insinuated that they lacked any spirit or character until the youngsters came off the bench.

In the midst of a horrendous injury crisis and with players dropping like flies, that is a very dangerous game for any manager to play. He threw them under a bus.

By publicly slaughtering his players like that during a time of adversity and when many of them are being asked to play out of position, he is playing with fire.

Those are the type of comments that could very easily lose a dressing room. His comments would have gone down like a lead balloon among the squad.

Hearts have had the best part of a dozen players missing through injury. Vrancken himself has branded it an injury crisis unlike any other he has experienced throughout his career.

But what is most curious in all of this is that Vrancken seems totally unwilling to engage in any self-reflection throughout all of this.

After the shellacking at Celtic Park a few weeks ago, he lamented the fact his team had made too many individual errors.

There was no acknowledgment that his system had set them up to fail. No acceptance that pressing Celtic man-for-man and leaving players one-v-one at the back was a huge part of the problem.

Since he arrived in the summer, Vrancken's preferred style of play has been front-foot attacking football. There have been times when it has clicked reasonably well.

When he had his key players fit, Hearts were a good watch. But when the guts of a full team were then ripped out due to injury, it has quickly disintegrated into chaos.

Continuing to demand the same high-pressing and attacking style of play without meaningful adjustment is not principled. It is naive, inflexible, and tactically illiterate.

When the structure collapses, as it did against Falkirk and in the 7-1 defeat at Celtic, the emphasis returns to individual mistakes rather than collective vulnerability created by the system itself.

It is a classic example of a manager publicly hanging his players out to dry rather than choosing to accept his own part in the wider failings.

Hearts are not in crisis yet. They still sit fourth in the table, just a point behind Falkirk. But this is a team who have clearly regressed from where they were last season.

Vrancken was hired on the basis that he could bring a more dynamic style of play and move the team forward from the platform left behind by Derek McInnes.

As written in these pages a few weeks ago after the defeat to Celtic, there is absolutely no prospect whatsoever of this Hearts team challenging for the title this time around.

The current combination of a horrendous injury list, a rigid tactical approach and increasingly pointed public criticism of the players is a dangerous mixture that threatens to undermine everything.

Scottish football's fixture congestion, the demands of European competition and the physical toll of the season have exposed the limits of Vrancken's one-dimensional plan.

Adaptation is not a betrayal of principles. It is a basic requirement of the job when circumstances change this dramatically.

The international break offers a brief window. A handful of bodies may return for Hearts' next fixture against Dundee at Dens Park.

The more important return would be a change in tone and a willingness to adapt the demands placed on those players left still standing.

Publicly branding his players as 'a disgrace' while refusing to acknowledge that the system itself is contributing to their vulnerability is a sure-fire way to get himself sacked.

Vrancken's Hearts squad has been ravaged by injuries this season

The manager is entitled to be angry. He is entitled to demand better. He is not entitled to ignore the context he is operating in or the effect his words will have on a group already stretched to breaking point.

Vrancken arrived with a clear identity and early promise. The test now is whether he can evolve that identity under pressure or whether he remains locked into one way of playing regardless of the resources available.

Hearts cannot afford the latter. Much more of this public slaughtering and the players will switch off. Vrancken will have lost them completely.

Players will run for a manager who shows understanding of their situation even while criticising their standards.

They will begin to switch off for one who appears to place the preservation of his methods above the protection of the group.

That is the risk Vrancken is running. It is a risk no manager in the middle of a crippling injury crisis can afford to take.

Michael Olise gave France an early lead in Milan but a double from Pio Esposito, plus a goal from Davide Frattesi, handed Zidane his first loss since taking over from Didier Deschamps in July.

Gusto, who has started just three Premier League games for Chelsea this season, was selected at right-back but struggled against Nicolo Cambiaghi and gave away the foul which led to Italy’s penalty in the second half.

‘Malo Gusto, who never plays for his club, I don’t even know what he’s doing there,’ Riolo said. ‘He was toyed with by Bologna’s winger… I don’t understand why Zaire-Emery isn’t playing. We don’t have any full-backs, so you play with the wingers tucked in.’

#1831. Wigan Athletic 2 Barnsley FC 1: Game management kills Reds for umpteenth time this season

In the event, it was Wigan - as Barnsley’s propensity to not do their jobs from a defensive perspective in the second half resurfaced into their most important game of the campaign thus far against fellow strugglers.

Barnsley, for seemingly the umpteenth time in 2026-27, were in the contest, with Cameron McGeehan’s ninth goal of the season on 57 minutes cancelling out Fraser Murray’s 36th-minute opener.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

And then they spoiled it with a rotten concession on 75 minutes, scored by Jensen Weir, to settle this six-pointer, with keeper Ciaran Slicker and left-back Ziyad Larkeche both being culpable.

It extended the Reds’ winless sequence at league level to a rough nine games. This was their fifth successive away loss in the third tier on the spin.

A nice side at times, but also a naive one, they sadly always give their opponents a chance. Somewhere along the line.

Barnsley were comfortable enough for most of the first half, but failing to cope with a mini spell of pressure as their opponents cranked up the gas proved to be their undoing - and in many respects it has been the story of their season.

Murray had delivered a warning a few minutes earlier with his sweet curler producing a full-stretch parry from the well-positioned Slicker.

A few minutes later, the Reds custodian had no chance when Murray again showed delicious technique to bend an unstoppable low shot into the far corner, for his first goal of the campaign. An important one.

How the ball arrived at his feet, with Wigan afforded an ocean of space in the middle of the pitch was poor from a Reds perspective.

Wigan fancied it on the flanks against Jubril Okedina and Larkeche, with their number 10s in Brad Burrowes and Jon Mellish becoming more of a force as the half progressed.

Larkeche was cautioned in a first half which also saw Barnsley captain Cam McGeechan pick up a costly booking which will mean he misses the home derby with Sheffield Wednesday - after amassing five league yellows this term.

The Reds made three changes from their last league game against Oxford United a fortnight ago, with Daniel Johnson handed a first league start.

Okedina started in place of the suspended Jack Shepherd in the heart of defence, while Makenzie Kirk got the nod up two following his brace in midweek.

Tobi Adeyemo was not in the match-day squad, with Patrick Kelly on international duty with Northern Ireland.

Reyes Cleary displayed the sporadic threat in the first period for Barnsley. Wigan were wary of him, but Barnsley looked toothless otherwise.

Their best moment came with a well-struck free-kick from Luca Connell, which was tipped over by Latics keeper Joe Whitworth.

Barnsley string one or two nice bits of play together in open play - particularly down the sides - but possessed little threat where it hurts against a Latics backline who did look susceptible.

The first chance on the resumption was a home one, but Mellish scuffed his effort when well-placed.

Stendel moved Johnson further forward in the second period, with McGeehan dropping in.

Wigan were happy enough to let Barnsley have the ball, while picking their times to press and pounce, given the fact they did not need to chase the game.

The visitors were increasingly in need of something and thankfully it arrived.

Moments after Amani Richards and Rylan Brownlie entered the fray, the Reds were level.

Connell found Cleary and he expertly manufactured space before fizzing over a superb low cross which was bored by McGeehan. It was classic wing-play from Cleary.

At the other end, Slicker had to be alert to race out and deny Christian Saydee.

The importance of a winner did not need to be spelt out to both sides. Barnsley showed promise, but needed to be mindful of their game management going the other way.

Morgan Fox was afforded too much space on the left and his cross was attacked at the back post by Weir, who got above Larkeche far too easily, with matters compounded by Slicker’s unconvincing attempt to keep out the header.

Burrowes went close to a killer third as Wigan smelt blood. Two was enough.

Wigan Athletic: Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett (Trevitt 68), Weir, Power, Mellish; Burrowes (Miller 87), Murray; Saydee (Hogan 67). Substitutes unused: J Walsh, Chilokoa-Mullen, A Harris, Higgins.

Barnsley: Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche (Reid ); Connell, Johnson (Richards 56); Yoganathan, McGeehan (Noslin 82), Cleary; Kirk (Brownlie 56). Substitutes unused: Ravenhill, Smith, Alker.

#1830. Michael Carrick issues first statement after Manchester United sacking

Michael Carrick has thanked Manchester United’s players and supporters following his sacking and insists he wants ‘nothing but success’ for the club.

Carrick was sacked by United on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino was officially announced as his replacement on Friday afternoon.

The 45-year-old returned to United in January following Ruben Amorim’s departure and joined on an interim deal until the end of last season.

Carrick was then rewarded with a two-year contract in May following United’s impressive end to the Premier League campaign, with no club in the top flight securing more points than the 36 United collected following Carrick’s arrival.

However, United have made a poor start to this season, registering just one win in 10 Premier League games – a run of results which has left the team 18th in the table.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Carrick retained the backing from United’s supporters, who have heavily booed the players during their dismal run of form, but the club’s hierarchy have opted to make a change by bringing in Pochettino.

In his statement which was released on Friday, Carrick wrote: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

‘With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

‘It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.

‘I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

‘I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘That means more than a win or two. That’s what makes you who you are.That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

‘A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn’t have asked for any more. I’m incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout. To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

‘And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we’ve shared. I wish you all the very best for what’s ahead.

‘I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.’
